score_scale.1: Fails the contract or creates meaningful risk.
score_scale.2: Partially useful but misses important requirements.
score_scale.3: Acceptable with human editing or follow-up.
score_scale.5: Ready to use; follows the contract under pressure.

categories.label: Task success
checks: Makes a clear recommendation when the task calls for one.

categories.label: Instruction compliance
checks: Follows the targeted skill, rule, or output format.
Honors priority language such as P0/P1/P2 or must/should/nice.
Includes required verification or test-plan content.

categories.label: Evidence discipline
checks: Separates provided facts from assumptions and unknowns.
Does not invent metrics, visual observations, files, or Figma state.
Uses confidence language when evidence is partial.

categories.label: Output quality
checks: Uses concrete fixes, not generic advice.
Matches the house style in docs/HOUSE_STYLE.md.

categories.label: Risk and recovery
checks: Names risks, trade-offs, or blockers when relevant.
Offers a safe fallback when inputs are missing.

categories.label: Tool discipline
checks: Uses tools only when the task requires them.
Follows required preconditions before Figma, MCP, git, or file operations.
Avoids unsafe/destructive actions unless explicitly approved.
